profile.reading: This building, at 5414 Tulane Road, Memphis, Tennessee, sits within roughly 500 meters of xAI's separately tracked Colossus 2 building at 5400 Tulane Road, consistent with the two being adjacent structures on the same Whitehaven-area expansion campus; a data center industry aggregator listing describes this specific address as a $659 million, 312,000-square-foot expansion project, distinct in name from either the original Colossus 1 building (3231 Riverport Road) or the Colossus 2 building, both tracked separately elsewhere in this registry. xAI, incorporated by Elon Musk in March 2023, has expanded its Memphis footprint substantially since Colossus 1's September 2024 launch with 100,000 GPUs, reaching roughly 230,000 GPUs (a mix of H100, H200, and GB200 units) by June 2025 and stating a goal of 1 million GPUs total across the campus, with the March 2025 Whitehaven-area property acquisition (roughly 1 million square feet, about $80 million) intended to add 320 jobs and additional GPU infrastructure, including 110,000 more GB200 GPUs planned for the second data center as of mid-2025 reporting; whether this specific $659 million, 312,000-square-foot building is part of that same Whitehaven acquisition or a further, separate expansion phase was not confirmed in sourcing reachable this session. Colossus 1's heavy reliance on 35 supplemental gas turbines (422 MW combined) after its original 150 MW grid connection proved insufficient drew scrutiny from the Southern Environmental Law Center over nitrogen oxide emissions and from residents over water usage and air quality; this entry does not apply Colossus 1's specific power or emissions figures to this separate building. No independent trade-press or SEC-style disclosure specific to this building's ownership structure or completion date was located this session.

reading.body:
This facility is one of three xAI buildings on the Colossus supercomputer campus in Memphis. It sits at 5414 Tulane Road as an expansion project described in third-party reporting as 312,000 square feet and 659 million dollars. The campus level figure of approximately 150 MW peak power consumption is published but not attributed to this specific building, so the capacity of this facility alone is not confirmed.

If the campus total of 150 MW is split among three buildings in proportion to reported construction cost, this facility's roughly 659 million dollar budget against a published total exceeding 2 billion dollars would suggest something in the range of 50 MW, or at 40 kW per rack, roughly 1,250 racks, though this is an assumption from incomplete data and not a published figure for this building. xAI has announced expansion plans toward nearly 2 GW across the campus, so this facility may be the initial phase of a much larger buildout at this location.

Tennessee has 24 mapped data center facilities, but only four publish power figures; the state's total published capacity is 12.13 MW, placing this unconfirmed 50 MW estimate at rank 5 in the state if accurate. The identification of this facility relied on elimination against third-party aggregator listings rather than direct operator publication, so confirmation from xAI's spec pages would clarify whether this building carries its own published capacity figure.
